newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves IOC 3.0 mln tonne distillation unit.
newsitem.headline: India approves IOC 3.0 mln tonne distillation unit.

text.p: India has approved a proposal by state-run Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) to set up a crude distillation unit with an annual capacity of three million tonnes annually, a government spokesman said on Saturday.
The decision was taken by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) on Friday, the spokesman said. The unit will be set up in the western state of Gujarat.
The CCEA has also approved the proposal to revamp the existing feed preparation unit and the fluidised catalytic cracking unit at the Gujarat refinery, the spokesman added.
The total cost of the project will be around 8.8 billion rupees, the spokesman said.

CCEA has also approved IOC's proposal to award contracts for four blocks and finalise production sharing contracts with successful bidders for joint exploration, he said. He gave no details of the blocks.

In 1995, the federal government invited bids for 28 blocks of which 18 were on-shore and ten off-shore. A total of 22 bids were received for seven blocks. Four have been finalised, the spokesman said.
